There are infinitely many connections on a Riemannian manifold, but exactly one is compatible with the metric. The **fundamental theorem of Riemannian geometry**: there exists a **unique** connection $
abla$ on $(M,g)$ satisfying the two conditions
(i) **metric compatibility**, $
abla g=0$, equivalently $Xg(Y,Z)=g(
abla_XY,Z)+g(Y,
abla_XZ)$, equivalently parallel transport preserves inner products and lengths;
(ii) **torsion-freeness** (symmetry), $
abla_XY-
abla_YX=[X,Y]$, i.e. $\Gamma^{i}{}_{jk}=\Gamma^{i}{}_{kj}$ in coordinates.
This unique $
abla$ is the **Levi-Civita connection** (Riemannian connection), and from here on $
abla$ always means it. Both conditions are indispensable: keeping only (i) one may add an arbitrary antisymmetric term, and keeping only (ii) one can still destroy metric compatibility (see the examples).

Uniqueness is a neat algebraic exercise. If $
abla$ and $	ilde
abla$ both satisfy (i) and (ii), then $D(X,Y)=
abla_XY-	ilde
abla_XY$ is a tensor (the non-tensorial terms cancel), (ii) gives $D(X,Y)=D(Y,X)$ and (i) gives $g(D(X,Y),Z)+g(Y,D(X,Z))=0$; adding the three cyclic permutations yields $2g(D(X,Y),Z)=0$ for all $Z$, so $D\equiv0$ and $
abla=	ilde
abla$. Rewriting the same computation so that it *solves* for $
abla$ gives the **Koszul formula** $2g(
abla_XY,Z)=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)+g(Y,[Z,X])+g(Z,[X,Y])-g(X,[Y,Z])$, whose right-hand side involves only $g$ and Lie brackets; hence it proves both existence (the object so defined satisfies (i) and (ii)) and uniqueness.

Setting $X=\partial_j$, $Y=\partial_k$, $Z=\partial_l$ in coordinates (all Lie brackets vanish) turns the Koszul formula into $2g(
abla_{\partial_j}\partial_k,\partial_l)=\partial_jg_{kl}+\partial_kg_{jl}-\partial_lg_{jk}$, whose solution is the **Christoffel symbol** $\Gamma^{i}{}_{jk}= rac{1}{2}g^{il}(\partial_jg_{lk}+\partial_kg_{lj}-\partial_lg_{jk})$ — the signs of the three terms are plus, plus, minus, and the index positions matter. It is symmetric in the lower indices (that is torsion-freeness) but **not a tensor**: under a change of coordinates it acquires an inhomogeneous term involving the second derivatives $\partial^{2}x/\partial x'{}^j\partial x'{}^k$. Consequently one can choose coordinates in which all $\Gamma$'s vanish at a given point (geodesic coordinates, a local inertial frame), but only at that point to first order; vanishing on a neighbourhood forces zero curvature. Finally, $
abla$ makes straightness and translation intrinsic: geodesics are the curves with $
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'=0$, in coordinates $\ddot x^{i}+\Gamma^{i}{}_{jk}\dot x^{j}\dot x^{k}=0$ (the same condition as vanishing geodesic curvature on a surface, now without any ambient space), and it also defines parallel transport along curves and the curvature $R(X,Y)Z=
abla_X
abla_YZ-
abla_Y
abla_XZ-
abla_{[X,Y]}Z$.

formulas.note: 仿射联络的两条公理：对第一个变量是函数线性的（所以它不是逐点的张量运算），对第二个变量是求导。
formulas.noteEn: The two axioms of an affine connection: function-linear in the first slot (so it is not a pointwise tensor operation) and a derivation in the second.

formulas.note: 度量相容与无挠；两条合起来唯一确定列维-奇维塔联络（黎曼几何基本定理），缺一不可。
formulas.noteEn: Metric compatibility and torsion-freeness; together they determine the Levi-Civita connection uniquely (the fundamental theorem), and neither can be dropped.

formulas.note: Koszul 公式：右端只含度量和李括号，构造性地给出存在性，并逐点确定 ∇ 的取值。
formulas.noteEn: The Koszul formula: the right-hand side uses only the metric and Lie brackets, giving existence constructively and determining $\nabla$ pointwise.

formulas.note: Christoffel 符号（三项符号：正、正、负）；右边等式是 $\nabla g=0$ 的坐标写法，两者等价。
formulas.noteEn: The Christoffel symbol (signs: plus, plus, minus); the second identity is $\nabla g=0$ in coordinates, an equivalent statement.

formulas.note: 测地线方程（内蕴形式 $\nabla_{\gamma'}\gamma'=0$ 的坐标写法）与沿曲线协变导数的坐标公式。
formulas.noteEn: The geodesic equation (coordinates of $\nabla_{\gamma'}\gamma'=0$) and the coordinate formula for the covariant derivative along a curve.

properties:
**存在且唯一**：同时满足度量相容与无挠的联络由 $g$ 唯一决定（Koszul／Christoffel 公式），并且它是等距不变量：等距变换 $f$ 把 $
abla^{g}$ 送到 $
abla^{h}$，即 $f_{*}
abla^{g}_{X}Y=
abla^{h}_{f_{*}X}f_{*}Y$。
**联络不是张量，但联络之差是张量**：$\nabla-\tilde\nabla$ 是 $(1,2)$ 型张量，唯一性等价于说这个差张量必为零；也正因为公理中的非张量项对任何联络都相同，两条公理才有可能「筛选」出唯一的一个。
**度量相容的几何含义**：平行移动是等距同构（保内积、保长度、保夹角），反之任何度量相容的联络都让 $g$ 在平行移动下不变；等价地，协变导数与用 $g$ 升降指标可以交换次序。

**无挠的几何含义**：等价于下指标对称 $\Gamma^{i}{}_{jk}=\Gamma^{i}{}_{kj}$，也等价于「二阶协变导数对称」：对任何函数 $f$ 有 $
abla_i
abla_jf=
abla_j
abla_if$（这就是「对称」一名的来历）。
**局部惯性系**：任一点可取测地（法）坐标使 $g_{ij}(p)=\delta_{ij}$、$\Gamma^{i}{}_{jk}(p)=0$（因为 $\Gamma$ 由 $\partial g$ 组成而 $\partial g(p)=0$）；但除非曲率为零，无法在整个邻域上同时做到——这正是 $\Gamma$ 不是张量的直接后果。
propertiesEn:
**Existence and uniqueness**: the connection that is both metric compatible and torsion-free is determined by $g$ alone (Koszul and Christoffel formulas), and it is an isometry invariant: an isometry $f$ carries $
abla^{g}$ to $
abla^{h}$, i.e. $f_{*}
abla^{g}_{X}Y=
abla^{h}_{f_{*}X}f_{*}Y$.

**A connection is not a tensor, but the difference of two connections is**: $\nabla-\tilde\nabla$ is a $(1,2)$-tensor, so uniqueness says exactly that this difference tensor vanishes; the fact that the non-tensorial terms are the same for every connection is what allows the two axioms to single out one connection.

**Geometric meaning of metric compatibility**: parallel transport is a linear isometry (preserving inner products, lengths and angles), and conversely any metric-compatible connection leaves $g$ invariant under parallel transport; equivalently, covariant differentiation commutes with raising and lowering indices.

**Geometric meaning of torsion-freeness**: it is equivalent to symmetry of the lower indices, $\Gamma^{i}{}_{jk}=\Gamma^{i}{}_{kj}$, and also to symmetry of second covariant derivatives of functions, $
abla_i
abla_jf=
abla_j
abla_if$ — the origin of the name.

**Local inertial frames**: at any point one can choose geodesic (normal) coordinates with $g_{ij}(p)=\delta_{ij}$ and $\Gamma^{i}{}_{jk}(p)=0$, because $\Gamma$ is built from $\partial g$ and $\partial g(p)=0$; unless the curvature vanishes this cannot hold on a whole neighbourhood, a direct consequence of $\Gamma$ not being a tensor.

examples.problem: 对单位球面度量 $g=d\theta^{2}+\sin^{2}\theta\,d\varphi^{2}$，用 Christoffel 公式算出全部联络系数、验证对称性，并判断赤道与一般纬线哪些是测地线。
examples.solution:
记 $(x^{1},x^{2})=(	heta,\varphi)$，$(g_{ij})=\operatorname{diag}(1,\sin^{2}	heta)$，$(g^{ij})=\operatorname{diag}(1,\sin^{-2}	heta)$，唯一的非零度规导数是 $\partial_{	heta}g_{\varphi\varphi}=2\sin	heta\cos	heta$。
$\Gamma^{	heta}{}_{\varphi\varphi}= rac{1}{2}g^{	heta	heta}(2\partial_{\varphi}g_{\varphi	heta}-\partial_{	heta}g_{\varphi\varphi})= rac{1}{2}\cdot1\cdot(-2\sin	heta\cos	heta)=-\sin	heta\cos	heta$；
$\Gamma^{\varphi}{}_{	heta\varphi}=\Gamma^{\varphi}{}_{\varphi	heta}= rac{1}{2}g^{\varphi\varphi}\partial_{	heta}g_{\varphi\varphi}= rac{1}{2\sin^{2}	heta}\cdot2\sin	heta\cos	heta=\cot	heta$；其余全为 $0$。下指标对称自动成立。
测地线方程为 $\ddot	heta-\sin	heta\cos	heta\,\dot\varphi^{2}=0$、$\ddot\varphi+2\cot	heta\,\dot	heta\dot\varphi=0$。
赤道 $	heta=\pi/2$、$\varphi=t$：$\dot	heta=\ddot	heta=0$，而 $\sin(\pi/2)\cos(\pi/2)=0$，两个方程都成立，故是测地线。
一般纬线 $	heta=	heta_0
eq\pi/2$、$\varphi=t$：第一个方程左边为 $-\sin	heta_0\cos	heta_0
eq0$，不成立，故不是测地线（它在球面上是「绕着极点转的小圆」，必须靠摩擦才能维持）。

examples.problem:
说明两个条件缺一不可。(1) 在 $\mathbb{R}^{3}$（欧氏度量）上令 $
abla_XY=D_XY+X	imes Y$，验证它度量相容但有挠；(2) 令 $
abla_XY=D_XY+\langle X,Yangle\xi$（$\xi
eq0$ 为固定向量），验证它无挠但不度量相容。
examples.solution:
(1) 因 $\langle X	imes Y,Zangle=\det(X,Y,Z)$ 关于 $(Y,Z)$ 反对称，所以 $$\langle X	imes Y,Zangle+\langle Y,X	imes Zangle=\det(X,Y,Z)+\det(Y,X,Z)=0,$$ 即 $X\langle Y,Zangle=\langle
abla_XY,Zangle+\langle Y,
abla_XZangle$，度量相容成立；但挠率 $T(X,Y)=
abla_XY-
abla_YX-[X,Y]=X	imes Y-Y	imes X=2X	imes Y
eq0$（取 $X,Y$ 线性无关）。
(2) 挠率 $T(X,Y)=\langle X,Yangle\xi-\langle Y,Xangle\xi=0$，无挠成立；而 $$(
abla_Xg)(Y,Z)=X\langle Y,Zangle-\langle D_XY+\langle X,Yangle\xi,Zangle-\langle Y,D_XZ+\langle X,Zangle\xiangle=-\langle X,Yangle\langle\xi,Zangle-\langle X,Zangle\langle Y,\xiangle,$$ 取 $Y=Z=\xi$ 得 $-2\langle X,\xiangle|\xi|^2
eq0$（当 $\xi
eq0$ 且 $X$ 不与 $\xi$ 垂直），故不度量相容。可见「唯一性」确实同时用到了两条公理。

nodes.title: 平行移动与和乐群
nodes.summary: 沿曲线协变导数为零的向量场给出切空间之间的线性等距同构；绕闭环平移一周所得变换构成的**和乐群**恰好测出曲率。
nodes.summaryEn: Vector fields with vanishing covariant derivative along a curve give linear isometries between tangent spaces; the transformations obtained around closed loops form the holonomy group, which measures curvature.
nodes.definition:
在黎曼流形上「把向量原封不动地搬过去」有确切含义：沿曲线 $\gamma$ 的向量场 $V$ 若满足 $$
abla_{\gamma'}V=0,$$ 就称为**平行向量场**。用坐标写出它是 $\dot V^{k}+\Gamma^{k}{}_{ij}\dot x^{i}V^{j}=0$：关于 $V$ 的一阶**线性**常微分方程组，因此给定初值 $V(t_0)$ 就有唯一解，并且可以延拓到整条曲线（线性方程组不会有奇点）。于是得到映射 $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M	o T_{\gamma(b)}M$，把初值送到终值，称为沿 $\gamma$ 的**平行移动**。

$P_\gamma$ 是线性同构，而且是**等距**同构：由度量相容性，$$ rac{d}{dt}g(V,W)=g(
abla_{\gamma'}V,W)+g(V,
abla_{\gamma'}W)=0,$$ 所以内积、长度、夹角一律保持不变（这正是 $
abla g=0$ 的几何内容）。平行移动还有函子性质 $P_{\gamma_2\circ\gamma_1}=P_{\gamma_2}\circ P_{\gamma_1}$、$P_{\gamma^{-1}}=P_{\gamma}^{-1}$，并且只依赖曲线的像与走向，与重参数化、途中停留无关。特别地，测地线的切向量自己就是平行向量场（测地线方程 $
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'=0$ 说的正是这件事），所以测地线在平行标架下就是「直线」。

然而 $P_\gamma$ 一般**依赖路径**：从 $p$ 到 $q$ 的两条不同曲线可以给出完全不同的结果。度量这种不可交换性的对象就是**和乐群**：固定基点 $p$，把所有以 $p$ 为基点的分段光滑闭环 $\gamma$（$\gamma(0)=\gamma(1)=p$）的平行移动收集起来，$$\mathrm{Hol}_p(M)=\{P_\gamma\}\subset O(T_pM),$$ 它是 $O(n)$ 的闭子群；若 $M$ 可定向，则 $\mathrm{Hol}_p(M)\subset SO(T_pM)$。把绕可缩闭环的部分记作 $\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$，它是单位分支（正规子群）。**关键联系（Ambrose–Singer 定理）**：和乐群的李代数由曲率张量生成——准确地说，由 $	au_\gamma^{-1}\circ R(v,w)\circ	au_\gamma$（$	au_\gamma$ 为沿任意曲线的平行移动）张成。因此
**曲率非零 ⟺ 平行移动依赖路径 ⟺ 限制和乐群非平凡**；
反过来曲率恒为零（平坦）⟺ 局部存在平行的正交标架 ⟺ $\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$ 平凡。要注意区分「限制」与「整体」：平坦流形的限制和乐群平凡，但整体和乐群仍可能非平凡，那是拓扑效应——平坦的 Möbius 带上绕一圈，横截方向正好翻转，$\mathrm{Hol}_p\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$。

球面是最直观的例子。$S^{2}_R$ 是常曲率 $K=1/R^{2}$ 的曲面，沿一条简单闭曲线平行移动一周，向量在 $T_pM$ 中旋转的角度恰为曲线所围区域的**立体角**，也等于 $\int_D K\,dA=\mathrm{area}(D)/R^{2}$（这正是 Gauss–Bonnet 定理的平行移动版本）。特别地，绕余纬 $	heta_0$ 的纬线一周，旋转角为 $2\pi(1-\cos	heta_0)$：$	heta_0$ 很小时旋转趋于 $0$（局部几乎平坦），$	heta_0=\pi/2$（赤道）时为 $2\pi$，与「恒等变换」相容。球面上的测地三角形（三个顶点用大圆连接）则给出旋转角 = 内角和 $-\pi$ = 角盈，例如顶点为北极与赤道上经度差 $\varphi$ 的两点时，旋转角正好是 $\varphi$。
nodes.definitionEn:
On a Riemannian manifold, transporting a vector faithfully along a curve means requiring the field $V$ along $\gamma$ to satisfy $
abla_{\gamma'}V=0$; such a $V$ is called **parallel**. In coordinates the equation reads $\dot V^{k}+\Gamma^{k}{}_{ij}\dot x^{i}V^{j}=0$, a first-order **linear** system of ODEs: given any initial vector $V(t_0)$ there is a unique solution, which extends to the whole curve. The resulting map $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M	o T_{\gamma(b)}M$ is the **parallel transport** along $\gamma$.

$P_\gamma$ is a linear isomorphism, and an **isometry**: metric compatibility gives $ rac{d}{dt}g(V,W)=g(
abla_{\gamma'}V,W)+g(V,
abla_{\gamma'}W)=0$, so inner products, lengths and angles are all preserved — that is the geometric content of $
abla g=0$. Parallel transport is functorial, $P_{\gamma_2\circ\gamma_1}=P_{\gamma_2}\circ P_{\gamma_1}$ and $P_{\gamma^{-1}}=P_{\gamma}^{-1}$, and depends only on the image and direction of the curve, not on its parametrization. In particular the tangent field of a geodesic is parallel along it (this is exactly $
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'=0$), so geodesics look like straight lines in a parallel frame.

In general, however, $P_\gamma$ **depends on the path**: two curves from $p$ to $q$ may give different answers. The object measuring this non-commutativity is the **holonomy group**: fix a base point $p$ and collect the transports around all piecewise smooth loops based at $p$ ($\gamma(0)=\gamma(1)=p$), obtaining $\mathrm{Hol}_p(M)=\{P_\gamma\}\subset O(T_pM)$, a closed subgroup of $O(n)$; if $M$ is orientable then $\mathrm{Hol}_p(M)\subset SO(T_pM)$. The part coming from contractible loops, $\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$, is the identity component (a normal subgroup). **The key link (Ambrose–Singer theorem)**: the Lie algebra of the holonomy group is generated by the curvature tensor — precisely, it is spanned by $	au_\gamma^{-1}\circ R(v,w)\circ	au_\gamma$, where $	au_\gamma$ denotes parallel transport along an arbitrary curve. Hence
**non-vanishing curvature ⟺ path-dependent parallel transport ⟺ non-trivial restricted holonomy**, and conversely zero curvature (flat) ⟺ existence of a locally parallel orthonormal frame ⟺ $\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$ trivial. The restricted and the full holonomy group must be distinguished: a flat manifold has trivial restricted holonomy but may still have non-trivial holonomy of topological origin — on a flat Möbius band one trip around flips the transverse direction, so $\mathrm{Hol}_p\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$.

Spheres are the most visual example. On $S^{2}_R$ of constant curvature $K=1/R^{2}$, transporting a vector once around a simple closed curve rotates it in $T_pM$ by the **solid angle** enclosed by the curve, equal to $\int_D K\,dA=\mathrm{area}(D)/R^{2}$ (the parallel-transport face of Gauss–Bonnet). In particular, a trip around the latitude circle of colatitude $	heta_0$ rotates vectors by $2\pi(1-\cos	heta_0)$: this tends to $0$ as $	heta_0	o0$ (locally almost flat) and equals $2\pi$ for the equator $	heta_0=\pi/2$, which is consistent with the identity. For a geodesic triangle the rotation angle is the angle sum minus $\pi$, the spherical excess; taking the north pole and two equatorial points of longitude difference $\varphi$ gives exactly $\varphi$.

formulas.note: 平行向量场的方程：一阶线性常微分方程组，给定初值向量有唯一解，可延拓到整条曲线。
formulas.noteEn: The equation of a parallel field: a first-order linear system, so any initial vector determines a unique solution extending over the whole curve.

formulas.note: 等距性与函子性：平行移动是切空间之间的线性等距同构，并对曲线复合、反向取逆都相容。
formulas.noteEn: Isometry and functoriality: parallel transport is a linear isometry between tangent spaces, compatible with composition and reversal of curves.

formulas.note: 和乐群：所有以 p 为基点的闭环的平行移动构成的群，是 $O(n)$ 的闭子群（可定向时落在 $SO(n)$ 里）。
formulas.noteEn: The holonomy group: all transports around loops based at $p$, a closed subgroup of $O(n)$ (contained in $SO(n)$ when $M$ is orientable).

formulas.note: Ambrose–Singer 定理：和乐群的李代数由曲率张量生成（$\tau_\gamma$ 为沿 $\gamma$ 的平行移动）；故 $R\equiv0\Leftrightarrow$ 限制和乐群平凡。
formulas.noteEn: Ambrose–Singer theorem: the Lie algebra of the holonomy group is spanned by curvature tensors transported around loops; hence $R\equiv0\Leftrightarrow$ trivial restricted holonomy.

formulas.note: 球面 $S^{2}_R$ 上的和乐角（向量绕简单闭曲线一周的旋转角）：等于所围区域的立体角，也等于面积除以 $R^{2}$。
formulas.noteEn: Holonomy angle on $S^{2}_R$ (rotation of a vector after one loop): it equals the enclosed solid angle, i.e. the enclosed area divided by $R^{2}$.

properties: $P_\gamma$ 只依赖曲线的像与走向，与参数化快慢无关；复合与求逆相容，因此以 $p$ 为基点的闭环的平行移动构成群。
$\mathrm{Hol}_p$ 是 $O(T_pM)$ 的闭子群（因而是紧李群）；$\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$（可缩闭环）是单位分支，且存在自然的满同态 $\pi_1(M,p)\to\mathrm{Hol}_p/\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$，所以单连通时 $\mathrm{Hol}_p=\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$，和乐只反映曲率。
$R\equiv0\iff$ 局部存在平行正交标架 $\iff\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p=\{1\}\iff g$ 局部等距于欧氏度量（Riemann 平坦）；但整体和乐群在平坦流形上仍可能非平凡（平坦 Möbius 带的和乐是 $\mathbb{Z}_2$），那是拓扑而非曲率造成的。
**无穷小版本**：绕以 $\varepsilon X,\varepsilon Y$ 为边的无穷小平行四边形一周，$$P_\gamma v=v-\varepsilon^{2}R(X,Y)v+O(\varepsilon^{3}),$$ 即曲率是「平行移动不可交换」的无穷小度量，这也是 Ambrose–Singer 定理的直观来源。
和乐群是分类黎曼流形的核心不变量（Berger 分类）：不可约且非局部对称的空间，其限制和乐群只能落在 $SO(n),\ U(n),\ SU(n),\ Sp(n),\ Sp(n)\cdot Sp(1),\ G_2,\ \mathrm{Spin}(7)$ 之中；例如 $\mathrm{Hol}\subset U(n)$ 恰好刻画 Kähler 流形。
propertiesEn: $P_\gamma$ depends only on the image and direction of the curve, not on how fast it is traversed; composition and reversal behave functorially, so transports around loops based at $p$ form a group.

$\mathrm{Hol}_p$ is a closed subgroup of $O(T_pM)$, hence a compact Lie group; $\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$ (contractible loops) is its identity component, and there is a natural surjection $\pi_1(M,p)\to\mathrm{Hol}_p/\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$, so for simply connected $M$ one has $\mathrm{Hol}_p=\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$ and holonomy reflects curvature only.

$R\equiv0\iff$ a locally parallel orthonormal frame exists $\iff\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p=\{1\}\iff g$ is locally isometric to the Euclidean metric (Riemann flat); the full holonomy may still be non-trivial on a flat manifold (a flat Möbius band has holonomy $\mathbb{Z}_2$), which is a topological rather than a curvature effect.

**Infinitesimal version**: going around the small parallelogram with sides $\varepsilon X,\varepsilon Y$ gives $P_\gamma v=v-\varepsilon^{2}R(X,Y)v+O(\varepsilon^{3})$, so curvature is the infinitesimal measure of the failure of parallel transports to commute — the intuition behind Ambrose–Singer.

The holonomy group is a central invariant in the classification of Riemannian manifolds (Berger): for an irreducible, non-locally-symmetric space the restricted holonomy must lie in one of $SO(n),\ U(n),\ SU(n),\ Sp(n),\ Sp(n)\cdot Sp(1),\ G_2,\ \mathrm{Spin}(7)$; for instance $\mathrm{Hol}\subset U(n)$ characterises Kähler manifolds.

plot.title: 球面上平行移动一周：向量旋转所围立体角

examples.problem: 在单位球面上，取测地三角形，顶点为北极 $N$ 与赤道上经度 $0$ 的点 $A$、经度 $\varphi$ 的点 $B$（三条边都是大圆）。求沿该三角形平行移动一周的净旋转角，并核对 $\Delta\theta=\mathrm{area}/R^{2}$。
examples.solution: 沿测地线平行移动时「向量与切线的夹角保持不变」，逐边追踪（在每段大圆上维持与切线的定角）可得：出发时取 $v_0=$ 第一条边的切向量，绕行一周回到 $N$ 后，$v$ 恰好是第三条边切向量的反向，而两条子午线在 $N$ 处的切向夹角为 $\varphi$，于是净旋转角 $=\varphi$。\n另一方面该三角形的三个内角为 $\varphi$（北极处）、$\pi/2$、$\pi/2$，内角和 $=\pi+\varphi$，角盈 $=\varphi$；又面积 $=\varphi R^{2}$（$R=1$ 时 $=\varphi$，恰好是经度区间所对应的「半个二角形」），故 $\mathrm{area}/R^{2}=\varphi$，与直接追踪一致。\n取 $\varphi=\pi/2$：这正是八分之一球面（面积 $\pi/2\approx1.571$），旋转角 $\pi/2=90^{\circ}$。可见平行移动不仅依赖路径，而且差异正好被「所围面积 $\times$ 曲率」量化。

examples.problem: 在（平坦）Möbius 带 $M=\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]/(t,s)\sim(t+1,1-s)$（配欧氏度量，曲率恒为 $0$）上，求基点 $p=(0,1/2)$ 处绕中心圆一周的平行移动，并解释这与 Ambrose–Singer 定理的关系。
examples.solution: 带上的度量为 $dt^{2}+ds^{2}$，Christoffel 符号全为零，故平行移动就是「在 $(t,s)$ 坐标下保持分量不变、再做粘合」。取环路 $\gamma(t)=(t,1/2)$，$t\in[0,1]$，初向量 $\partial_s$：分量保持不变地到达 $(1,1/2)$，但粘合 $(1,1/2)\sim(0,1-1/2)=(0,1/2)$ 是把 $(t,s)\mapsto(t+1,1-s)$，其微分为 $ds\mapsto-ds$，于是 $P_\gamma(\partial_s)=-\partial_s$，而 $P_\gamma(\partial_t)=\partial_t$。所以 $P_\gamma=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$ 是反射，$\mathrm{Hol}_p\cong\mathbb{Z}_2\neq\{1\}$。\n这说明定理中的「曲率非零 $\Leftrightarrow$ 和乐非平凡」必须加「限制和乐群」：这里的环路不可缩（$\pi_1(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ 由它生成），它对应的是和乐的拓扑部分；限制和乐群 $\mathrm{Hol}^{0}_p$ 仍然平凡，与曲率为零完全一致。

nodes.title: 指数映射与单射半径
nodes.titleEn: The Exponential Map and Injectivity Radius
nodes.summary: exp_p 把切空间的直线映为流形上过 p 的测地线，在 0 附近是局部微分同胚；单射半径是它保持单射的最大半径，等于到割迹的距离。
nodes.summaryEn: exp_p maps straight lines in the tangent space to geodesics through p and is a local diffeomorphism near 0; the injectivity radius is the largest radius on which it stays injective and equals the distance to the cut locus.
nodes.definition:
测地线的存在唯一性使我们能「用切向量造曲线」：对 $v\in T_pM$，记 $\gamma_v$ 为满足 $\gamma(0)=p$、$\gamma'(0)=v$ 的极大测地线，定义 $$\exp_p(v)=\gamma_v(1)$$ （只要 $\gamma_v$ 至少定义到 $t=1$）。由测地线的齐次性 $\exp_p(tv)=\gamma_v(t)$，也就是把 $T_pM$ 中的直线 $t\mapsto tv$ 映为 $M$ 中从 $p$ 出发、初速度 $v$ 的测地线。几何图像是「把切空间展开到流形上」；以 $\exp_p$ 为坐标卡的坐标叫**测地坐标（法坐标）**。若 $M$ 完备，则 $\exp_p$ 在整个 $T_pM$ 上有定义，且 $M=\exp_p(T_pM)$（Hopf–Rinow）：测地线能走到任何地方。

局部性质很容易得到：由 $ igl(d\exp_p igr)_0(v)= rac{d}{dt} ig|_0\exp_p(tv)=\gamma_v'(0)=v$ 知 $(d\exp_p)_0=\mathrm{id}$，于是反函数定理告诉我们 $\exp_p$ 在 $0$ 的某个邻域上是到 $p$ 的邻域的**微分同胚**。用这个微分同胚当坐标，就有 $g_{ij}(0)=\delta_{ij}$、$\partial_kg_{ij}(0)=0$，从而 $\Gamma^{i}{}_{jk}(0)=0$：在这点一阶看来流形就是欧氏的（局部惯性系）。必须强调这只是**一点**的性质：$\Gamma$ 在邻域中一般不为零，它在邻域中为零才意味着平坦。

这套结构的核心是 **Gauss 引理**：对 $v\in T_pM$ 与 $w\in T_v(T_pM)\cong T_pM$，$$ igl\langle (d\exp_p)_v(v),\,(d\exp_p)_v(w) igrangle=\langle v,wangle_p.$$ 特别地取 $w=\lambda v$ 得 $|(d\exp_p)_v(v)|=|v|$，而且 $w\perp v$ 时像也垂直。于是：**$\exp_p$ 的径向测地线与测地球面 $\{\exp_p(w):|w|=r\}$ 处处正交**，并且径向测地线是**极小**的——在 $\exp_p$ 是微分同胚的范围内，径向测地线段的长度就等于 $|v|$，也就是 $d igl(p,\exp_pv igr)=|v|$。这是「测地线局部极小」的标准证明，也是测地极坐标下度量能写成 $g=dr^{2}+g_{\alpha eta}(r,	heta)d	heta^{\alpha}d	heta^{ eta}$（无 $dr\,d	heta$ 交叉项）的原因。

**单射半径**衡量 $\exp_p$ 能保持单射的范围：$$\mathrm{inj}(p)=\sup\{r>0:\ \exp_p\ 	ext{在}\ B(0,r)\subset T_pM\ 	ext{上单射}\},\qquad \mathrm{inj}(M)=\inf_{p}\mathrm{inj}(p).$$ 当 $r<\mathrm{inj}(p)$ 时 $\exp_p:B(0,r)	o B(p,r)$ 不仅是单射，而且是**微分同胚**（单射性会排除临界点），像恰是度量球 $B(p,r)=\{q:d(p,q)<r\}$：测地球与度量球一致。这里要分清「单射」与「微分同胚」：单射只要求两条不同的测地线不在球内相撞，微分同胚还要切映射处处可逆，条件更强；但在测地球这个情形下二者等价。更精细的关系是 $$\mathrm{inj}(p)=d igl(p,C(p) igr),$$ 其中 $C(p)$ 是 $p$ 的**割迹**——径向测地线不再极小、或被另一条测地线追上的那些点的集合；而 $\mathrm{inj}(p)$ 不超过到第一个**共轭点**的距离。球面 $S^{2}_R$ 是标准例子：$\mathrm{inj}(p)=\pi R$，$\exp_p$ 在 $|v|=\pi R$（对径点）处奇异，切映射秩降为 $n-1$。
nodes.definitionEn:
Existence and uniqueness of geodesics let us build curves from tangent vectors: for $v\in T_pM$ let $\gamma_v$ be the maximal geodesic with $\gamma(0)=p$, $\gamma'(0)=v$, and set $\exp_p(v)=\gamma_v(1)$ (whenever $\gamma_v$ reaches $t=1$). By homogeneity of geodesics, $\exp_p(tv)=\gamma_v(t)$: the straight line $t\mapsto tv$ in $T_pM$ is sent to the geodesic through $p$ with initial velocity $v$. The geodesic (normal) coordinates are the coordinates given by $\exp_p$. If $M$ is complete then $\exp_p$ is defined on all of $T_pM$ and $M=\exp_p(T_pM)$ (Hopf–Rinow): geodesics reach every point.

The local behaviour is immediate: since $(d\exp_p)_0(v)= rac{d}{dt} ig|_0\exp_p(tv)=\gamma_v'(0)=v$, we have $(d\exp_p)_0=\mathrm{id}$, so by the inverse function theorem $\exp_p$ is a **diffeomorphism** from a neighbourhood of $0$ onto a neighbourhood of $p$. In these coordinates $g_{ij}(0)=\delta_{ij}$ and $\partial_kg_{ij}(0)=0$, hence $\Gamma^{i}{}_{jk}(0)=0$: to first order at that point the manifold looks Euclidean (a local inertial frame). This is a statement about **one point** only; $\Gamma$ generally does not vanish nearby, and vanishing on a neighbourhood would mean flatness.

The heart of the structure is **Gauss's lemma**: for $v\in T_pM$ and $w\in T_v(T_pM)\cong T_pM$, $\langle (d\exp_p)_v(v),(d\exp_p)_v(w)angle=\langle v,wangle_p$. Taking $w=\lambda v$ gives $|(d\exp_p)_v(v)|=|v|$, and $w\perp v$ gives orthogonality of the images. Consequently the **radial geodesics of $\exp_p$ are everywhere orthogonal to the geodesic spheres** $\{\exp_p(w):|w|=r\}$, and radial geodesics are **minimising**: wherever $\exp_p$ is a diffeomorphism, a radial segment has length $|v|$, i.e. $d(p,\exp_pv)=|v|$. This is the standard proof that geodesics are locally minimising, and the reason the metric in geodesic polar coordinates has the form $g=dr^{2}+g_{\alpha eta}(r,	heta)d	heta^{\alpha}d	heta^{ eta}$ with no $dr\,d	heta$ cross terms.

The **injectivity radius** measures how far $\exp_p$ stays injective: $\mathrm{inj}(p)=\sup\{r>0:\exp_p\ 	ext{is injective on}\ B(0,r)\subset T_pM\}$, and $\mathrm{inj}(M)=\inf_p\mathrm{inj}(p)$. For $r<\mathrm{inj}(p)$, $\exp_p:B(0,r)	o B(p,r)$ is not merely injective but a **diffeomorphism** (injectivity rules out critical points), and its image is exactly the metric ball $B(p,r)=\{q:d(p,q)<r\}$: geodesic balls and metric balls agree. Here injectivity and being a diffeomorphism must be distinguished: injectivity only says that two distinct geodesics do not meet inside the ball, whereas being a diffeomorphism also requires the differential to be invertible everywhere — a stronger requirement, although for such balls the two are equivalent. More precisely, $\mathrm{inj}(p)=d(p,C(p))$, where $C(p)$ is the **cut locus** of $p$, the set of points where radial geodesics stop being minimising or get caught by another geodesic; and $\mathrm{inj}(p)$ does not exceed the distance to the first **conjugate point**. The sphere $S^{2}_R$ is the standard example: $\mathrm{inj}(p)=\pi R$, and $\exp_p$ is singular at $|v|=\pi R$ (the antipode), where its differential has rank $n-1$.

formulas.note: 指数映射的定义与齐次性；在原点处的微分为恒等，故由反函数定理得到局部微分同胚。
formulas.noteEn: Definition and homogeneity of the exponential map; its differential at $0$ is the identity, so the inverse function theorem gives a local diffeomorphism.

formulas.note: Gauss 引理；推论是径向测地线与测地球面正交，且 $|(d\exp_p)_v(v)|=|v|$（测地线局部极小）。
formulas.noteEn: Gauss's lemma; the corollary is that radial geodesics are orthogonal to geodesic spheres and $|(d\exp_p)_v(v)|=|v|$ (local minimality).

formulas.note: 单射半径的定义及其与割迹、共轭点的关系；$r<\mathrm{inj}(p)$ 时 $\exp_p:B(0,r)\to B(p,r)$ 是微分同胚。
formulas.noteEn: Definition of the injectivity radius and its relation to the cut locus and conjugate points; for $r<\mathrm{inj}(p)$ the map $\exp_p:B(0,r)\to B(p,r)$ is a diffeomorphism.

formulas.note: 测地（法）坐标的性质：$p$ 点处度量是欧氏的、联络系数为零；极坐标下无 $dr\,d\theta$ 交叉项（Gauss 引理的直接推论）。
formulas.noteEn: Properties of geodesic (normal) coordinates: Euclidean at $p$ with vanishing connection coefficients, and no $dr\,d\theta$ cross terms in polar form (a corollary of Gauss's lemma).

formulas.note: 法坐标下体积密度的展开（Ric 为 Ricci 张量）：这是 Bishop–Gromov 体积比较的出发点；球面上取 $S^{2}_R$ 可验证：$R\sin(r/R)=r\bigl(1-r^{2}/(6R^{2})+\cdots\bigr)$。
formulas.noteEn: Expansion of the volume density in normal coordinates (Ric is the Ricci tensor), the seed of Bishop–Gromov volume comparison; on $S^{2}_R$ it reads $R\sin(r/R)=r(1-r^{2}/(6R^{2})+\cdots)$.

properties: $\exp:TM\to M$ 光滑，$\exp_p$ 光滑依赖 $p$；$\exp_p$ 在 $v$ 处奇异（切映射不可逆）当且仅当 $\exp_p(v)$ 是 $p$ 的**共轭点**，共轭点的距离总不小于 $\mathrm{inj}(p)$。
**测地球 = 度量球**：$r<\mathrm{inj}(p)$ 时 $\exp_p$ 把 $B(0,r)$ 微分同胚地映到 $B(p,r)=\{q:d(p,q)<r\}$；$\exp_p$ 是单射当且仅当没有径向测地线在球内相撞，这解释了为什么单射半径与「最短测地线」是同一件事的两个侧面。
**完备性**：$\exp_p$ 对某个（因而每个）点定义在整个 $T_pM$ 上 $\iff$ $(M,d)$ 完备 $\iff$ 有界闭集紧；此时任意两点都由一条极小测地线连接（Hopf–Rinow），且 $\exp_p$ 满射。
**测地极坐标**：Gauss 引理给出 $g=dr^{2}+g_{\alpha\beta}(r,\theta)d\theta^{\alpha}d\theta^{\beta}$，$r$ 就是到 $p$ 的黎曼距离；由此可推出径向测地线在 $r<\mathrm{inj}(p)$ 内极小，反过来共轭点之外一般不再极小。

**例子与整体量**：$S^{2}_R$ 有 $\mathrm{inj}=\pi R$；平坦环面 $\mathbb{R}^{2}/\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ 每点 $\mathrm{inj}=1/2$（等于最短闭测地线长度之半）；双曲空间 $\mathrm{inj}=\infty$（Cartan–Hadamard：$\exp_p$ 是整体微分同胚）。紧流形的 $\mathrm{inj}(M)=\inf_p\mathrm{inj}(p)>0$，这是紧性的一个非平凡推论。
propertiesEn: $\exp:TM\to M$ is smooth and $\exp_p$ depends smoothly on $p$; $\exp_p$ is singular at $v$ (non-invertible differential) exactly when $\exp_p(v)$ is a **conjugate point** of $p$, and the distance to a conjugate point is never smaller than $\mathrm{inj}(p)$.

**Geodesic balls are metric balls**: for $r<\mathrm{inj}(p)$, $\exp_p$ maps $B(0,r)$ diffeomorphically onto $B(p,r)=\{q:d(p,q)<r\}$; injectivity fails exactly when two radial geodesics collide inside the ball, which is why the injectivity radius and shortest geodesics describe the same phenomenon.

**Completeness**: $\exp_p$ is defined on all of $T_pM$ for one (hence every) point $\iff$ $(M,d)$ is complete $\iff$ closed bounded sets are compact; then any two points are joined by a minimising geodesic (Hopf–Rinow) and $\exp_p$ is surjective.

**Geodesic polar coordinates**: Gauss's lemma yields $g=dr^{2}+g_{\alpha\beta}(r,\theta)d\theta^{\alpha}d\theta^{\beta}$ with $r$ the Riemannian distance to $p$; hence radial geodesics minimise for $r<\mathrm{inj}(p)$, while beyond a conjugate point they generally do not.

**Examples and global quantities**: $S^{2}_R$ has $\mathrm{inj}=\pi R$; the flat torus $\mathbb{R}^{2}/\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ has $\mathrm{inj}=1/2$ at every point (half the length of the shortest closed geodesic); hyperbolic space has $\mathrm{inj}=\infty$ (Cartan–Hadamard: $\exp_p$ is a global diffeomorphism). For a compact manifold $\mathrm{inj}(M)=\inf_p\mathrm{inj}(p)>0$, a non-trivial consequence of compactness.

plot.title: 测地极坐标中 r = √(x²+y²) 的等值线

examples.problem: 在单位球面 $S^{2}$ 上取 $p=$ 北极，写出 $\exp_p$ 的显式公式，证明它在 $|v|=\pi$ 处奇异，并求出 $\mathrm{inj}(p)$。
examples.solution:
单位球面上从北极出发、初速度 $v$ 的测地线是 $\gamma_v(t)=\cos igl(t|v| igr)p+\sin igl(t|v| igr) rac{v}{|v|}$（验证：$|\gamma|=1$，$\gamma(0)=p$，$\gamma'(0)=v$，且加速度平行于位置向量，故是测地线），于是 $$\exp_p(v)=\cos|v|\,p+\sin|v|\, rac{v}{|v|}.$$
当 $|v|=\pi$ 时 $\exp_p(v)=-p$ 对球面 $|v|=\pi$ 上**所有** $v$ 都成立，显然不单射；又由 Gauss 引理 $|(d\exp_p)_v(v)|=|v|=\pi
eq0$，而切于球面 $|v|=\pi$ 的方向全被映到同一点，故 $d\exp_p$ 在 $|v|=\pi$ 处处秩为 $n-1=1$，奇异。
$|v|<\pi$ 时单射：若 $\exp_p(v)=\exp_p(w)$，比较与 $p$ 的内积得 $\cos|v|=\cos|w|$，在 $(0,\pi)$ 上单调故 $|v|=|w|$，再比较垂直于 $p$（即 $T_pM$ 中的切向分量）的部分，得 $\sin|v|\, rac{v}{|v|}=\sin|w|\, rac{w}{|w|}$，由 $\sin|v|=\sin|w|
e0$ 得 $v=w$。所以 $\mathrm{inj}(p)=\pi$（半径 $R$ 的球面为 $\pi R$），割迹就是单个点 $\{-p\}$。

examples.problem: 求平坦环面 $\mathbb{R}^{2}/\mathbb{Z}^{2}$（商度量 $dx^{2}+dy^{2}$）上每点的单射半径，并说明为什么它与点无关。
examples.solution:
在平坦环面上测地线就是直线在商映射 $\pi:\mathbb{R}^{2}	o\mathbb{R}^{2}/\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ 下的像，于是 $\exp_p(v)=p+v mod\mathbb{Z}^{2}$（把 $v$ 视为 $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ 中的向量）。
$\exp_p(v)=\exp_p(w)\iff v-w\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}$。若 $|v|<r,\ |w|<r$ 且 $v
eq w$，则 $v-w$ 是非零格向量，其欧氏长度至少为 $1$（最短非零格向量长度），而 $|v-w|\le|v|+|w|<2r$；因此只要 $2r\le1$，即 $r\le1/2$，就不会有碰撞：$\exp_p$ 在 $B(0,1/2)$ 上单射。
反之取 $r>1/2$，令 $v= igl(	frac12+\epsilon,0 igr)$，$w= igl(-	frac12-\epsilon,0 igr)$，则 $v-w=(1,0)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ 但 $v
eq w$，说明不单射。所以 $\mathrm{inj}(p)=1/2$，与 $p$ 无关（平坦度量的平移不变性）；它也等于最短闭测地线长度 $1$ 的一半，割迹是基本域边界在环面上的像。

nodes.title: 弧长第一变分
nodes.summary: 长度泛函沿变分族的一阶导数公式；固定端点时为 −∫⟨V, ∇_γ′γ′⟩dt，由此「测地线 = 临界点」「最短曲线必是测地线」，但反之不成立。
nodes.summaryEn: The first derivative of the length functional along a variation: with fixed endpoints it equals −∫⟨V, ∇_{γ'}γ'⟩dt, giving "geodesic = critical point" and "minimisers are geodesics", while the converse fails.
nodes.definition:
把曲线看作泛函的自变量。给定曲线 $\gamma:[a,b]	o M$，一个**变分**是一族曲线 $\gamma_s$（$|s|<\varepsilon$，$\gamma_0=\gamma$），使 $(s,t)\mapsto\gamma_s(t)$ 光滑；若对所有 $s$ 都有 $\gamma_s(a)=\gamma(a)$、$\gamma_s(b)=\gamma(b)$，就称它是**固定端点**的变分。**变分场** $V(t)= rac{\partial\gamma_s}{\partial s} ig|_{s=0}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ 描述曲线「往哪儿动」，反过来任意光滑场 $V$（沿 $\gamma$，端点处为零）都来自某个固定端点变分。第一变分就是 $s\mapsto L(\gamma_s)$ 在 $s=0$ 的导数：它衡量曲线微小变形时长度的一阶变化，用来找出「最可能最短」的曲线——长度泛函的临界点。

推导只需要两件事：度量的相容性，以及协变导数在 $s$ 与 $t$ 两个方向上的可交换（由无挠性保证）。对**单位速率**的曲线 $|\gamma'|=1$（长度与参数化无关，一般曲线先按弧长重参数化），得到**第一变分公式**：$$ rac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}L(\gamma_s)=-\int_a^b g igl(V,
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma' igr)\,dt;$$ 端点不固定时要加上边界项：$$ rac{dL}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}=-\int_a^b g igl(V,
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma' igr)\,dt+g igl(V(b),\gamma'(b) igr)-g igl(V(a),\gamma'(a) igr),$$ 边界项不能漏：它正是「曲线端点移动」带来的收益。**注意负号**：$
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'$ 表示曲线向外「加速」的方向，而加速的方向恰恰是长度一阶减少的方向。能量泛函 $E= rac12\int|\gamma'|^{2}dt$ 有完全相同的公式，而且不需要单位速率假设（这就是变分问题中常用 $E$ 代替 $L$ 的原因）；对固定端点两者临界条件也相同。

由此立刻得到几个结论。
**(i) 测地线恰是临界点**：曲线 $\gamma$ 满足 $
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'=0$ 当且仅当对一切固定端点的变分都有 $ rac{dL}{ds} ig|_{s=0}=0$。必要性显然；充分性取 $V=f\,
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'$（$f\ge0$ 光滑、支集在内部），得 $\int f igl|
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma' igr|^{2}dt=0$，故 $
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'\equiv0$。
**(ii) 最短曲线必是测地线**（这个蕴含方向不能反）：若 $\gamma$ 是按弧长参数化的极小曲线，则对任何固定端点变分有 $L(\gamma_s)\ge L(\gamma)$，故 $ rac{dL}{ds} ig|_{s=0}=0$，由 (i) 即得 $
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'=0$。
**(iii) 逆命题不成立**：测地线只是临界点，未必极小。以单位球面为例，赤道上的测地线 $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t,0)$，$t\in[0,3\pi/2]$ 的端点是 $(1,0,0)$ 与 $(0,-1,0)$，它们的最短连线只有 $\pi/2$，而这条测地线长 $3\pi/2$；真正极小的只是「走短弧」的那条。极小性只能在局部成立（在单射半径内由 Gauss 引理保证），一旦越过第一个共轭点（球面上是对径点），测地线就不再极小——这要靠第二变分（index form）来判断。
nodes.definitionEn:
Treat a curve as the variable of a functional. Given $\gamma:[a,b]	o M$, a **variation** is a family $\gamma_s$ ($|s|<\varepsilon$, $\gamma_0=\gamma$) with $(s,t)\mapsto\gamma_s(t)$ smooth; it is a **fixed-endpoint** variation if $\gamma_s(a)=\gamma(a)$ and $\gamma_s(b)=\gamma(b)$ for all $s$. The **variation field** $V(t)= rac{\partial\gamma_s}{\partial s} ig|_{s=0}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ says where the curve moves, and conversely every smooth field $V$ along $\gamma$ vanishing at the endpoints arises from such a variation. The first variation is the derivative of $s\mapsto L(\gamma_s)$ at $s=0$: the first-order change of length under a small deformation, used to detect the critical points of the length functional.

Only two facts are needed: metric compatibility, and the symmetry of covariant differentiation in the $s$- and $t$-directions (guaranteed by torsion-freeness). For a curve parametrized by **unit speed**, $|\gamma'|=1$ (length is parametrization-invariant, so reparametrize by arclength first), the **first variation formula** reads $ rac{d}{ds} ig|_{s=0}L(\gamma_s)=-\int_a^b g(V,
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma')\,dt$; without fixed endpoints one must add the boundary terms, $ rac{dL}{ds} ig|_{s=0}=-\int_a^b g(V,
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma')\,dt+g(V(b),\gamma'(b))-g(V(a),\gamma'(a))$. The boundary terms may not be dropped: they are exactly the gain obtained by moving the endpoints. Mind the **minus sign**: $
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'$ points in the direction in which the curve accelerates, and accelerating lowers the length to first order. The energy $E= rac12\int|\gamma'|^{2}dt$ obeys the same formula without any unit-speed hypothesis (the classical reason to work with $E$ instead of $L$), and for fixed endpoints the two have the same critical points.

Three consequences follow at once.
(i) **Geodesics are exactly the critical points**: $
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'=0$ holds if and only if $ rac{dL}{ds} ig|_{s=0}=0$ for every fixed-endpoint variation. Necessity is obvious; for sufficiency take $V=f\,
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'$ with a smooth $f\ge0$ compactly supported in the interior and get $\int f|
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'|^{2}dt=0$, hence $
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'\equiv0$.
(ii) **A minimiser is a geodesic** (this implication cannot be reversed): if $\gamma$ is a minimising curve parametrized by arclength, then $L(\gamma_s)\ge L(\gamma)$ for every fixed-endpoint variation, so $ rac{dL}{ds} ig|_{s=0}=0$ and (i) applies.
(iii) **The converse fails**: a geodesic is only a critical point, not necessarily a shortest curve. On the unit sphere the geodesic $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t,0)$ for $t\in[0,3\pi/2]$ joins $(1,0,0)$ to $(0,-1,0)$, whose shortest connection has length $\pi/2$ only, whereas this geodesic has length $3\pi/2$; only the short arc minimises. Minimality is local (inside the injectivity radius, by Gauss's lemma), and beyond the first conjugate point — the antipode on a sphere — geodesics cease to minimise, which is decided by the second variation (the index form).

formulas.note: 变分与变分场：固定端点意味着变分场在两端为零；反之任何这样的光滑场都由某个固定端点变分实现。
formulas.noteEn: Variation and variation field: fixed endpoints mean $V$ vanishes at both ends, and conversely every such smooth field comes from a fixed-endpoint variation.

formulas.note: 固定端点的第一变分公式：只通过「加速度」$\nabla_{\gamma'}\gamma'$ 出现，负号不能丢；$\gamma$ 需以单位速率参数化。
formulas.noteEn: First variation formula for fixed endpoints: only the acceleration $\nabla_{\gamma'}\gamma'$ appears and the minus sign is essential; $\gamma$ must have unit speed.

formulas.note: 一般端点的完整公式：两个边界项必须保留，它们是横截条件（极小曲线与自由端点所在子流形正交）的来源。
formulas.noteEn: Full formula with free endpoints: the two boundary terms are indispensable and give the transversality condition (a minimiser meets the free-endpoint submanifold orthogonally).

formulas.note: 临界点判据：测地线就是长度（与能量）泛函的临界点，这就是测地线方程的变分来源。
formulas.noteEn: Critical-point criterion: geodesics are precisely the critical points of length (and energy) — the variational origin of the geodesic equation.

formulas.note: 能量泛函有同样的第一变分且不需要单位速率假设；柯西–施瓦茨的等号当且仅当 $|\gamma'|$ 为常数（极小化 $E$ 时会自动如此）。
formulas.noteEn: The energy has the same first variation and needs no unit-speed assumption; Cauchy–Schwarz is an equality exactly when $|\gamma'|$ is constant (automatic for $E$-minimisers).

properties: 第一变分只依赖**变分场** $V$：两个不同但变分场相同的变分有相同的一阶导数，于是变分问题被翻译成「对一切 $V$ 的积分等式」。由此得到**测地线 ⟺ 临界点**（对 $L$ 与 $E$ 都成立）：这既是测地线方程的变分来源，也与「直接解二阶 ODE」殊途同归。
**最短 ⟹ 测地线**（正确的蕴含方向）；**逆命题不成立**：测地线只保证一阶变分为零。球面上长度超过 $\pi$ 的大圆弧、柱面上绕过多圈的螺旋线都不是极小曲线。
边界项的用处：端点可沿子流形 $N$ 自由滑动时，取 $V$ 切于 $N$，由 $\frac{dL}{ds}\big|_{s=0}=0$ 得 $g\bigl(V,\gamma'\bigr)=0$ 对一切 $V\in T_qN$ 成立，即**极小曲线必与 $N$ 正交**（横截条件）。
第一变分只给出必要条件；要判断测地线是否极小需看第二变分（index form）：在第一个共轭点之前测地线极小，之后不再极小，$\mathrm{inj}(p)$ 正是这个临界位置。
两种泛函的比较：$L$ 与参数化无关但在 $\gamma'=0$ 处不可导、第一变分要求单位速率；$E$ 没有根号、公式干净，且 $E$ 的临界点自动是常速测地线。
propertiesEn: The first variation depends only on the **variation field** $V$: two different variations with the same field have the same first derivative, which turns the problem into an integral identity for all $V$. This yields **geodesic ⟺ critical point** (for both $L$ and $E$), the variational origin of the geodesic equation — reached equally by solving the second-order ODE directly.

**Minimiser ⟹ geodesic** (the correct direction); **the converse is false**: a geodesic only guarantees vanishing first variation, and great-circle arcs longer than $\pi$ on a sphere, or helices winding several times on a cylinder, are not minimising.

Use of the boundary terms: if an endpoint is free to move along a submanifold $N$, choosing $V$ tangent to $N$ in $\frac{dL}{ds}\big|_{s=0}=0$ gives $g(V,\gamma')=0$ for all $V\in T_qN$, i.e. a **minimiser meets $N$ orthogonally** (transversality).

The first variation gives only a necessary condition; minimality is decided by the second variation (index form): a geodesic minimises up to the first conjugate point and no longer afterwards, and $\mathrm{inj}(p)$ marks exactly that threshold.

Comparing the two functionals: $L$ is parametrization-invariant but non-smooth where $\gamma'=0$ and its formula requires unit speed, whereas $E$ has no square root, has clean formulas and its critical points are automatically constant-speed geodesics.

**证明**：设 $\gamma:[a,b]	o M$ 按弧长参数化（$|\gamma'|=1$）且实现最短，即对任何同端点曲线 $\sigma$ 都有 $L(\gamma)\le L(\sigma)$。对任意固定端点变分 $\gamma_s$，函数 $s\mapsto L(\gamma_s)$ 在 $s=0$ 取到最小值，故 $ rac{dL}{ds} ig|_{s=0}=0$。由第一变分公式，$-\int_a^b g(V,
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma')\,dt=0$ 对一切满足 $V(a)=V(b)=0$ 的光滑场 $V$ 成立。取 $V=f\,
abla_{\gamma'}\gamma'$，其中 $f\ge0$ 光滑、支集含于 $(a,b)$ 内部：$$0=-\int_a^b f\, igl|

**反例**：单位球面上的测地线 $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t,0)$，$t\in[0,3\pi/2]$，端点为 $P=(1,0,0)$ 与 $Q=(0,-1,0)$。$P,Q$ 是单位向量且夹角为 $\pi/2$，故球面距离 $d(P,Q)=\pi/2$，最短曲线是反方向的那段大圆弧（长度 $\pi/2$）；而 $L(\gamma)=3\pi/2>\pi/2$。所以该测地线不极小。另一个典型例子是柱面上的螺旋线：它处处是测地线，但绕的圈数越多越不可能是最短路径。

nodes.title: 黎曼曲率张量
nodes.summary: 度量与联络的二阶信息：R(X,Y)Z = ∇_X∇_YZ − ∇_Y∇_XZ − ∇_{[X,Y]}Z 度量「二阶协变导数不可交换」的程度，而 R ≡ 0 恰好刻画局部平坦。
nodes.summaryEn: The second-order invariant of the metric: R(X,Y)Z = ∇_X∇_YZ − ∇_Y∇_XZ − ∇_{[X,Y]}Z measures the failure of second covariant derivatives to commute, and R ≡ 0 characterises local flatness.
nodes.definition:
平坦空间里「先沿 $X$ 求导、再沿 $Y$ 求导」与反过来做结果相同；一般流形上这个次序不能交换。**黎曼曲率张量**就是这种不可交换性的度量。定义（本批一律采用这个约定）：$$R(X,Y)Z=
abla_X
abla_YZ-
abla_Y
abla_XZ-
abla_{[X,Y]}Z,$$ 最后一项李括号项 $-
abla_{[X,Y]}Z$ **不能漏**：少了它，$R$ 在一点的取值会依赖 $Y$ 在邻域内的变化，那就不是张量。加上它以后 $R$ 对三个变元都是 $C^{\infty}(M)$-线性的，是 $(1,3)$ 型张量场。等价的说法：记二阶协变导数 $
abla^2_{X,Y}Z=
abla_X
abla_YZ-
abla_{
abla_XY}Z$，则 $$R(X,Y)Z=
abla^2_{X,Y}Z-
abla^2_{Y,X}Z,$$ 即**曲率就是二阶协变导数的交换子**（差额恰好由 $
abla_{
abla_XY}Z-
abla_{
abla_YX}Z=
abla_{[X,Y]}Z$ 补上）。
**指标约定（本批所有公式都按它写，请务必注意次序）**：把分量定义为 $R(\partial_i,\partial_j)\partial_k=R^{l}{}_{ijk}\partial_l$，即**前两个下指标是求导方向、第三个才是被求导的向量**，于是 $$R^{l}{}_{ijk}=\partial_i\Gamma^{l}{}_{jk}-\partial_j\Gamma^{l}{}_{ik}+\Gamma^{l}{}_{im}\Gamma^{m}{}_{jk}-\Gamma^{l}{}_{jm}\Gamma^{m}{}_{ik}.$$ 结构是「两个导数项 + 两个乘积项」，符号按 $i\leftrightarrow j$ 配对成反对称——这正是 $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ 在分量上的样子。$\Gamma$ 本身不是张量（换坐标会多出二阶导数项），而两个导数项的非张量部分与两个 $\Gamma\Gamma$ 项恰好抵消，所以 $R$ 是张量：曲率可以测量，联络不可以。用度规拉下上指标得**全协变形式** $$R_{ijkl}=g_{lm}R^{m}{}_{ijk}=\langle R(\partial_i,\partial_j)\partial_k,\partial_langle.$$ 许多教材把被求导的向量写在**第一个**下指标（把 $\langle dx^{l},R(\partial_j,\partial_k)\partial_iangle$ 记作 $R^{l}{}_{ijk}$），那时坐标公式与一切缩并式都要跟着轮换下指标——例如里奇张量，本文次序写作 $R_{jl}=R^{i}{}_{ijl}$，另一套次序写作 $R_{jl}=R^{i}{}_{jil}$。查文献、抄公式时这里最容易出错。
几何意义有两个层次。定性地说，$R\equiv0$ **当且仅当局部平坦**：$R$ 恒为零时每点附近存在坐标使 $g_{ij}=\delta_{ij}$（等价地：存在局部平行的正交标架，平行移动与路径无关）。要注意「局部」二字：平坦环面 $\mathbb{T}^{n}=\mathbb{R}^{n}/\mathbb{Z}^{n}$ 满足 $R\equiv0$，但整体并不等距于欧氏空间。定量的版本是测地坐标展开：在 $p$ 点的测地（法）坐标 $x$ 下（基在 $p$ 点取单位正交）$$g_{ij}(x)=\delta_{ij}- rac{1}{3}R_{mijn}(p)\,x^{m}x^{n}+O(|x|^{3}),\qquad R_{mijn}=\langle R(\partial_m,\partial_i)\partial_j,\partial_nangle.$$ 也就是说：$\Gamma(p)=0$ 总能在一点做到（一阶信息可消去），而度量偏离欧氏的第一个非平凡项（二阶项）完全由曲率决定；$R(p)
eq0$ 的邻域无论换什么坐标都消不掉。
nodes.definitionEn:
In flat space it does not matter whether one differentiates first in the direction $X$ and then in the direction $Y$ or the other way round; on a general manifold the two orders do not commute. The **Riemann curvature tensor** measures exactly this failure. Definition (the convention used throughout this batch): $R(X,Y)Z=
abla_X
abla_YZ-
abla_Y
abla_XZ-
abla_{[X,Y]}Z$, where the Lie bracket term must not be dropped: without it the value of $R$ at a point would depend on the behaviour of $Y$ nearby, so the expression would not be tensorial. With it, $R$ is $C^{\infty}(M)$-linear in all three arguments, i.e. a $(1,3)$-tensor field. Equivalently, writing $
abla^2_{X,Y}Z=
abla_X
abla_YZ-
abla_{
abla_XY}Z$, one has $R(X,Y)Z=
abla^2_{X,Y}Z-
abla^2_{Y,X}Z$: the curvature is the commutator of second covariant derivatives (the difference $
abla_{
abla_XY}Z-
abla_{
abla_YX}Z=
abla_{[X,Y]}Z$ closes the gap).
**Index convention (all formulas in this batch follow it).** We write $R(\partial_i,\partial_j)\partial_k=R^{l}{}_{ijk}\partial_l$, i.e. the first two lower indices are the differentiation directions and the third is the vector being differentiated, so that $R^{l}{}_{ijk}=\partial_i\Gamma^{l}{}_{jk}-\partial_j\Gamma^{l}{}_{ik}+\Gamma^{l}{}_{im}\Gamma^{m}{}_{jk}-\Gamma^{l}{}_{jm}\Gamma^{m}{}_{ik}$. The pattern is "two derivative terms plus two product terms", with signs paired so that the expression is antisymmetric in $i\leftrightarrow j$ — the component form of $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$. The Christoffel symbols are not a tensor (under a change of coordinates a term with second derivatives appears), but their non-tensorial parts cancel in $R$, so $R$ is a tensor: curvature is measurable, a connection is not. Lowering the index with the metric gives the fully covariant form $R_{ijkl}=g_{lm}R^{m}{}_{ijk}=\langle R(\partial_i,\partial_j)\partial_k,\partial_langle$. Many textbooks put the differentiated vector in the **first** lower index (writing $\langle dx^{l},R(\partial_j,\partial_k)\partial_iangle$ as $R^{l}{}_{ijk}$); then the coordinate formula and every contraction must be permuted accordingly — for instance the Ricci tensor reads $R_{jl}=R^{i}{}_{ijl}$ in our ordering and $R_{jl}=R^{i}{}_{jil}$ in the other. This is the most common source of sign errors when copying formulas from the literature.
Geometrically, $R\equiv0$ **if and only if the manifold is locally flat**: near every point there are coordinates with $g_{ij}=\delta_{ij}$ (equivalently, a locally parallel orthonormal frame exists and parallel transport is path independent). The word "locally" matters: the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{n}=\mathbb{R}^{n}/\mathbb{Z}^{n}$ has $R\equiv0$ but is not isometric to Euclidean space. Quantitatively, in geodesic (normal) coordinates $x$ at $p$, with an orthonormal basis at $p$, one has $g_{ij}(x)=\delta_{ij}- rac{1}{3}R_{mijn}(p)x^{m}x^{n}+O(|x|^{3})$ with $R_{mijn}=\langle R(\partial_m,\partial_i)\partial_j,\partial_nangle$. Thus $\Gamma(p)=0$ can always be arranged at a single point (first-order information can be removed), while the first non-trivial deviation of the metric from the Euclidean one — the quadratic term — is determined by the curvature; if $R(p)
eq0$, no choice of coordinates can make the neighbourhood Euclidean.

formulas.note: 定义（约定）：李括号项不能漏，否则不是张量；等价地，曲率是二阶协变导数的交换子。
formulas.noteEn: The definition (our convention): the $[X,Y]$ term must not be dropped, otherwise the expression is not tensorial; equivalently, curvature is the commutator of second covariant derivatives.

formulas.note: $R(\partial_i,\partial_j)\partial_k=R^{l}{}_{ijk}\partial_l$ 的坐标公式：两项导数 + 两项乘积，关于 $i\leftrightarrow j$ 反对称；换另一套下指标次序的文献请重新核对。
formulas.noteEn: Coordinate formula for $R(\partial_i,\partial_j)\partial_k=R^{l}{}_{ijk}\partial_l$: two derivative terms plus two product terms, antisymmetric in $i\leftrightarrow j$; re-check it when using sources with the other index order.

formulas.note: 全协变形式与最基本的反对称性 $R_{ijkl}=-R_{jikl}$；$R(X,X)Y=0$。
formulas.noteEn: The fully covariant form and the basic antisymmetry $R_{ijkl}=-R_{jikl}$; in particular $R(X,X)Y=0$.

formulas.note: 测地坐标下的展开：$p$ 点处可以取 $g=\delta$、$\Gamma=0$，而度量偏离欧氏的第一个非平凡项就是曲率（$R_{mijn}=\langle R(\partial_m,\partial_i)\partial_j,\partial_n\rangle$）。
formulas.noteEn: Expansion in geodesic (normal) coordinates: at $p$ one may arrange $g=\delta$ and $\Gamma=0$, and the first non-trivial deviation of the metric from Euclidean is the curvature ($R_{mijn}=\langle R(\partial_m,\partial_i)\partial_j,\partial_n\rangle$).

formulas.latex: R\equiv0\iff\Gamma\ \text{可局部消去}\iff g\ \text{局部等距于欧氏度量}\iff\ \text{存在局部平行正交标架}
formulas.note: 局部平坦判据：四个条件等价；注意只是「局部」，平坦环面就是整体不等距于欧氏空间的例子。
formulas.noteEn: Local flatness criterion: these four conditions are equivalent; note that it is only local — the flat torus is not globally isometric to Euclidean space.

properties: **张量性与线性性**：$R$ 是 $(1,3)$ 型张量，对三个变元 $C^{\infty}(M)$-线性；固定 $X,Y$ 时 $Z\mapsto R(X,Y)Z$ 是切空间上的线性算子，而 $(X,Y)\mapsto R(X,Y)$ 反对称（所以 $R(X,X)Y=0$）。$\Gamma$ 不是张量而 $R$ 是张量，这就是「曲率是几何量、联络是坐标产物」的准确含义。
**局部而非整体的平坦性**：$R\equiv0$ 只保证局部欧氏。整体上还可能有拓扑与和乐效应：平坦环面、平坦 Möbius 带都满足 $R\equiv0$，但前者 $\pi_1\cong\mathbb{Z}^{2}$、后者的和乐群是 $\mathbb{Z}_2$。反过来，$R$ 只要在一点非零，就永远消不掉（$R$ 是张量，零是坐标无关的）。
**与平行移动的关系（几何意义）**：绕以 $\varepsilon X,\varepsilon Y$ 为边的无穷小平行四边形平行移动一周，向量变为 $$v-\varepsilon^{2}R(X,Y)v+O(\varepsilon^{3}),$$ 所以曲率是「平行移动不可交换」的无穷小度量；Ambrose–Singer 定理把这句直观升级为：限制和乐群的李代数由 $R$ 生成。
**与测地线的关系**：沿测地线 $\gamma$ 的 Jacobi 场满足 $J''+R(J,\gamma')\gamma'=0$；在常曲率 $k$ 的空间里化为 $J''+kJ=0$——$k>0$ 时解振荡（测地线互相聚焦），$k\leq0$ 时解单调增长（测地线永久发散）。曲率的符号就是测地线聚焦与发散的符号。
**对称性预告**：$R$ 绝不是任意的 $(1,3)$ 张量：它满足五条代数对称性与第二比安基恒等式（见 curvature-symmetries），独立分量只有 $\frac{n^{2}(n^{2}-1)}{12}$ 个——$n=2,3,4$ 时分别是 $1,6,20$。
propertiesEn: **Tensoriality and linearity**: $R$ is a $(1,3)$-tensor, $C^{\infty}(M)$-linear in all three arguments; for fixed $X,Y$ the map $Z\mapsto R(X,Y)Z$ is a linear operator on the tangent space, while $(X,Y)\mapsto R(X,Y)$ is antisymmetric (hence $R(X,X)Y=0$). Christoffel symbols are not tensors whereas $R$ is — the precise meaning of "curvature is geometric, a connection is an artefact of coordinates".

**Locally but not globally flat**: $R\equiv0$ only guarantees a locally Euclidean metric. Globally there can be topological and holonomy effects: the flat torus and the flat Möbius band both satisfy $R\equiv0$, yet the former has $\pi_1\cong\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ and the latter has holonomy group $\mathbb{Z}_2$. Conversely, if $R\neq0$ at one point it can never be removed (being a tensor, its vanishing is coordinate independent).

**Relation to parallel transport**: going around the infinitesimal parallelogram with sides $\varepsilon X,\varepsilon Y$ sends a vector to $v-\varepsilon^{2}R(X,Y)v+O(\varepsilon^{3})$, so curvature is the infinitesimal measure of the failure of parallel transports to commute; the Ambrose–Singer theorem upgrades this picture: the Lie algebra of the restricted holonomy group is generated by $R$.

**Relation to geodesics**: a Jacobi field along a geodesic $\gamma$ satisfies $J''+R(J,\gamma')\gamma'=0$, which in a space of constant curvature $k$ becomes $J''+kJ=0$: for $k>0$ solutions oscillate (geodesics refocus), for $k\leq0$ they grow monotonically (geodesics diverge forever). The sign of the curvature is the sign of geodesic focusing.

**Preview of the symmetries**: $R$ is far from an arbitrary $(1,3)$-tensor: it satisfies five algebraic symmetries and the second Bianchi identity (see curvature-symmetries) and therefore has only $\frac{n^{2}(n^{2}-1)}{12}$ independent components — namely $1,6,20$ for $n=2,3,4$.
